Render every track of a MIDI on its own, MIDI ports, and experimental analytic phase rotation by @DixelU.

## What's new

- **Per-track rendering.** Render every track of a MIDI on its own, as a folder of stems (`--tracks all -o folder`) or summed into one file (`--tracks all --merge -o song.flac`). In the guided renderer it's menu item 2. `kestrel tracks song.mid` shows what each track holds.
- **Huge files work.** A MIDI with tens of thousands of tracks and billions of notes renders end to end, per track and merged.
- **MIDI ports.** A track that sets a port gets sixteen channels of its own, so multi-port MIDIs no longer mix their parts together. Kestrel keeps sixteen ports, A to P, like Domino.
- **Experimental analytic phase rotation, `--phase-mode analytic`, by @DixelU in #1.** Stacked copies of the same note get different phases, so they stop summing in lockstep. Off by default, and it needs extra memory and a few minutes to prepare. See the [guide](https://github.com/thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi/blob/main/docs/analytic-phase-rotation.md).
- **Faster renders.** A normal render is a little quicker, because building voices now uses several CPU cores.
- **The done screen lists the flags** a render ran with.
- **For GUI builders.** Per-track renders report their tracks in the API's `per_track` field. See [API.md](https://github.com/thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi/blob/main/API.md).

## Fixes

- **`--gpu-backend` with a number**, such as `--gpu-backend 5`, now points you to `--adapter 5`, which is what picks a card from the guided renderer's list. A wrong backend name is refused straight away instead of after the soundfont loads.
- **Extras no longer lists the null test** in the downloads, which don't include it.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `kestrel-1.2.0-windows-x64.zip` | Windows 10/11 |
| `kestrel-1.2.0-macos-universal.dmg` | macOS 11 or newer (Apple silicon and Intel) |
| `kestrel-1.2.0-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 or newer) |

- **Windows:** unzip and double-click `kestrel.exe`. If SmartScreen warns you, click **More info → Run anyway**.
- **macOS:** copy `kestrel` out of the dmg. The first time you open it, allow it under **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**.
- **Linux:** extract it and run `./kestrel` in a terminal. You need a Vulkan driver.

The macOS build hasn't been tested yet. If you try it, please [open an issue](https://github.com/thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi/issues) and tell us how it went.
